chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so,' until he counted nine (ancestors). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed, you are the tenth of them in the Fire.'

key_terms.فُلَانُ: So-and-so (a placeholder name used when the specific name is omitted or generic)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say to a man who boasted about his nine ancestors?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, a man enumerates nine ancestors to boast of his noble lineage, to which the Prophet (peace be upon him) declares him the tenth in Hellfire, illustrating that pride in ancestry is a spiritual defect. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on *al-waqf* (stopping at the Prophet's statement) as a complete proof, showing that *nasab* (lineage) alone does not confer salvation without accompanying piety (*taqwa*). It serves as a critique of tribal arrogance, a prevalent social vice in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia, aligning with the Prophetic tradition that true nobility is measured by character and deeds rather than genealogy.
